```{r data}
# Every figure below is measured, not illustrative. Sources:

#   dev/NO-EXP-11-search.log   the 100-case search run
#   dev/NO-EXP-12-score.log    recoverability, the taxonomy, the match rate
#   dev/NO-EXP-13-calpacket.log + dev/NO-EXP-14-calib.log   the human head-to-head
#   dev/NO-TIER-EXPERIMENT.md  the design and the full read-out
# Embedded as literals so this vignette builds without the reference, a
# cascade run, or an API key. Regenerate with dev/adjudicate-1*.R.

status_tbl <- data.frame(
  status = c("YES", "MAYBE", "NO", "OOS"),
  identities = c(2979L, 1044L, 845L, 35L),
  share = c("60.76%", "21.29%", "17.23%", "0.71%"),
  meaning = c("accepted automatically",
              "candidates surfaced, none decisive",
              "nothing surfaced, or all of it vetoed",
              "flagged out of sample before matching"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

no_shape <- data.frame(
  shape = c("retrieved something, scored below the floor",
            "no blocking pass produced any pair at all"),
  identities = c(725L, 120L),
  `in the baseline's denominator` = c("yes", "**no**"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

recover_tbl <- data.frame(
  step = c("an EIN was established at all",

  n = c("34 of 91", "**33 of 91**"),
  share = c("37.4%", "**36.3%**"),
  ci = c("", "[27.1%, 46.5%]"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

why_tbl <- data.frame(
  cause = c("offered to the scorer and rejected", "never offered at all"),
  diagnosis = c("a scoring / threshold failure", "a blocking / retrieval failure"),
  n = c("26", "11"),
  share = c("70.3%", "29.7%"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

miss_tbl <- data.frame(
  hypothesis = c("LEGAL_NAME_DIFFERS", "TRUNCATED", "DBA_OR_TRADE_NAME",
                 "PARENT_OR_CHAPTER", "ACRONYM", "GEOGRAPHY_WRONG",
                 "PROGRAM_NAMED", "PLAIN_MISS", "TYPO"),
  `never offered` = c(2L, 1L, 3L, 0L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 0L, 2L),
  offered = c(7L, 6L, 4L, 5L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 0L),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

class_tbl <- data.frame(
  `entity_class` = c("INDIVIDUAL", "NONPROFIT", "FOREIGN", "GOVERNMENT",
                     "GROUP_SUBORDINATE", "AGGREGATE", "CHURCH",
                     "PROGRAM_OR_EVENT", "FISCALLY_SPONSORED", "FOR_PROFIT"),
  n = c(39L, 27L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 3L, 3L, 2L, 1L, 1L),
  share = c("42.9%", "29.7%", "5.5%", "5.5%", "5.5%", "3.3%", "3.3%",
            "2.2%", "1.1%", "1.1%"),
  `~of 845` = c(362L, 251L, 46L, 46L, 46L, 28L, 28L, 19L, 9L, 9L),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

group_tbl <- data.frame(
  group = c("not an organisation the BMF could ever hold",
            "a real body the BMF should list",
            "a real body with no exemption of its own",
            "could not be identified at all"),
  n = c("53 of 91", "33 of 91", "6 of 91", "0 of 91"),
  share = c("**58.2%**", "**36.3%**", "6.6%", "0.0%"),
  ci = c("[48.0%, 67.8%]", "[27.1%, 46.5%]", "[3.1%, 13.6%]", ""),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

flag_tbl <- data.frame(
  signal = c("`looks_personal` is TRUE",
             "filed status code reads `individual`"),
  `catches` = c("11 of 39", "19 of 39"),
  recall = c("28.2%", "48.7%"),
  `false positives` = c("**0 of 11**", "not measured here"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

den_tbl <- data.frame(
  denominator = c("result frame", "in scope", "whole file"),
  n = c(4748L, 4868L, 4903L),
  what = c("identities with at least one scored candidate",
           "every identity the cascade should have resolved",
           "every identity in the population file"),
  `YES alone` = c("62.74%", "**61.20%**", "60.76%"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

rate_tbl <- data.frame(
  numerator = c("YES alone",
                "YES + recovered NO",
                "YES + cleared MAYBE",
                "YES + cleared MAYBE + recovered NO"),
  `on 4,868 in scope` = c("61.20%", "67.49%", "77.11%", "**83.40%**"),

```

An automated cascade either finds a grant recipient in the IRS Business Master
File or it does not. [Adjudicating the MAYBE
tier](adjudicating-maybe.html) is about the cases where it found several
candidates and could not choose. This one is about the cases where it found
nothing worth offering — and the first thing to say is that most of them are
not matching failures at all.

**Of 91 randomly drawn NO identities, 53 are payees the Business Master File
could never contain.** Individuals collecting scholarships, businesses,
government bodies, foreign organisations, and placeholders like `SEE SCHEDULE
ATTACHED`. Only 33 are organisations the file should list and the cascade
missed. The honest floor — real bodies with no exemption of their own — is 6.

## The tier this is about

```{r}
tab(status_tbl, col.names = c("status", "identities", "share of 4,903", "meaning"))
```

### 845, not 725

The published baseline reports **725** NO. `pf_status()` reports **845**, and
the gap is the interesting part.

```{r}
tab(no_shape)
```

`pf_status()` runs over every identity in the file. The tiered result runs only
over identities that got at least one scored candidate. 120 in-scope
identities never reached the result frame because no blocking pass produced any
pair at all — and so the baseline's denominator of 4,748 **excludes the cases
retrieval failed on hardest**.

```{r}
tab(den_tbl)
```

On the in-scope denominator the same run is 61.20%, not 62.74%. That is not a
defect in the arm; it is a statement about which figure answers which
question. A match rate cannot drop the grants its retrieval step never reached.
Everything below is reported against 4,868.

## Why there is one arm and no cost frontier

The MAYBE experiment compared a cheap model, an expensive one, and the
expensive one with web search, because all three could answer its question: the
correct EIN was already in the candidate set 71% of the time, so a reviewer
confined to the packet had something real to decide.

Here it is not. A NO case has no candidate worth offering, so **when there is
an answer it is outside the packet 100% of the time.** A model without search
can only report that the filed name does not resemble the records already
rejected, which is what the cascade said. So there is one arm, it has search,
and no cheaper strategy is benchmarked because none applies.

That asymmetry is itself a finding: the MAYBE tier supports a cost/quality
frontier and the NO tier does not.

## What a reviewer is given

The filed record — name, street, city, state, ZIP, stated purpose, amount, tax
year, and the foundation's own recipient-status text, all uncontrolled filer
free text. The filing foundation, as context. And then one of two things:

- **no candidate retrieved** (12 of the 100 cases): nothing to show, the
  reviewer works from the filed record alone
- **the rejected near-misses, with their scores** (88 cases): the records the
  cascade found and declined

The near-misses are shown deliberately. In the prior hand audit the correct
record had *already been offered* in most recoverable cases, so hiding them
would hide the dominant mechanism.

They are also a trap, and the schema is built around it. An EIN read off a
near-miss row is in the reference **by construction** — it got there because
the blocker pulled it out of the reference — so counting it as evidence that
the reference covers this tier is circular. Every verdict therefore records
whether its EIN came from the web or from a candidate row, and the headline
uses web-sourced EINs only.

As it happened, **all 34 EINs in the estimation stratum were web-sourced and
none was read off a candidate row**, so the guard had nothing to exclude. That
was not guaranteed; it is why it was built.

## How much of the tier is recoverable

```{r}
tab(recover_tbl, col.names = c("", "n", "share", "95% Wilson"))
```

That projects to **~306 of the 845** NO identities, [229, 393].

"Recoverable" here means: the investigation established an EIN from an outside
source, and that EIN is in the reference. It is a mechanical set-membership
test — the model never saw the reference and was told so. It is **not** a
verified match: an EIN can be in the reference and still belong to the wrong
organisation. The head-to-head below is the only check on that.

### Is the right EIN already in the reference?

This is the question that decides whether the NO tier is a coverage problem or
a name problem.

| | in the reference |
|---|---|
| estimation stratum | 33 of 34 — 97.1% |
| both strata | **37 of 38 — 97.4%** [86.5%, 99.5%] |

The single exception is `COMMONWEALTH UNIV OF PENN`, EIN 23-2738930, which the
model classed `GOVERNMENT` — a Pennsylvania state university. A governmental
unit is not an exempt organisation, so the file is **correct** to omit it.

**Zero genuine coverage gaps in 38 independently established EINs.** The
earlier audit found 21 of 21 on a narrower population; this confirms it on the
production tier at nearly double the n. Widening the reference will not shrink
this residual, because the reference already contains it.

## Why the cascade missed them

For the 37 recoverable cases, was the correct EIN ever put in front of the
scorer? Every scored pair is cached, so this is a lookup rather than a replay
of the blocker.

```{r}
tab(why_tbl)
```

Where it *was* offered, the score the comparator gave the correct row was a
median of **0.360**, ranging 0.080 to 0.622, against a review floor of 0.65.
Only 2 of 26 reached even 0.60.

So the dominant failure is not retrieval. In 70% of recoverable cases the right
record was in hand and ranked far below the floor.

```{r}
tab(miss_tbl)
```

Two patterns are worth naming.

**`TYPO` is never retrieved.** `THE WESMINSTER SCHOOL` and `COCORDIA
UNIVERSITY` each scored *no* candidates at all. A misspelling inside the one
distinctive token destroys the only key an inverted name-token index could have
used. No comparator can rescue a case that never reaches it.

**`PARENT_OR_CHAPTER` is always retrieved and always underscored.** Four of the
five are `SALVATION ARMY` and `YOUNG LIFE` at 0.08 — a name that cannot
discriminate between hundreds of real records, where the geography term
correctly refuses to break the tie. These should *not* be forced through:
loosening there buys wrong EINs.

The two call for opposite fixes, which is why reporting them as one "name
resolution" number would be useless.

## What lives outside the BMF, and why

```{r}
tab(class_tbl)
```

Rolled up by whether a record should exist at all:

```{r}
tab(group_tbl, col.names = c("", "n", "share", "95% Wilson"))
```

### Not an organisation (58.2%)

The largest group in the tier by a wide margin. 39 individuals — almost all
scholarship payments to named students — plus 5 government bodies (a high
school, a public elementary school, a county fire and rescue department, a
state university, a university research institute), 5 foreign organisations (a
Polish foundation, UNIDROIT, a UK charity, a BC society, the ICRC), 3 aggregate
placeholders, and 1 for-profit.

These reached the matching path, where they can only fail or match something
wrong. **They are a denominator problem, not a matching problem.**

And the pipeline's own signals largely did not catch them:

```{r}
tab(flag_tbl)
```

Every case `looks_personal` flagged really is an individual — 11 of 11, no
false positives — and it misses 28 of 39. A precise, low-recall flag is the
easy kind to fix: nothing needs to become more conservative, the 202-name
given-name list simply has to get longer. Seven payees that are not
organisations at all are affirmatively coded `public_charity` by the filed
status field, which is why that field cannot be trusted on its own.

### A real body with no exemption of its own (6.6%)

The honest floor. Two churches (`SEVIER HEIGHTS BAPTIST CHURCH`, `ST AGNES
CHURCH`), which are exempt without applying and need not file; a diocesan high
school under a group ruling; one fiscally sponsored project; and two named
events. There is no EIN to find, so no amount of matching recovers these.

At 6.6% this is **much smaller** than the prior audit's 12-in-100 estimate for
the same category. The floor is a few percent, not a tenth.

### Could not be identified at all (0%)

Search identified something in every one of the 91 cases. The prior audit,
which searched 46 of its 67 adjudicated cases, had 10 "no such organisation
traceable". With search applied to every case that category disappears.

### Why `entity_class` and `bmf_expectation` are separate fields

The `INTERNATIONAL COMMITTE OF THE RED CROSS` case earns the distinction. The
model classed it `FOREIGN`, which is right — it is Swiss — and
`bmf_expectation` `LISTED`, which is also right, because it holds a US
exemption record. The EIN it reported is in the reference.

Collapsing "what the entity is" into "should a record exist" would have scored
that case wrong whichever way it collapsed. A Scout troop is a subordinate and
is not listed; a Salvation Army area command is a subordinate and is. They are
different questions.

## Does a human agree?

Almost everything above is the model's judgement, so it needs a check against
something other than the model's own confidence.

An earlier hand audit adjudicated 67 NO cases. Re-keyed on the filed recipient
name, 63 of them are still NO identities in this arm, so the same arm was run
over exactly those 63 and the two sides compared. Both judged the same
organisations from the same filed record; the only difference is who judged.

```{r}
agree_tbl <- data.frame(
  class = c("not an organisation", "a real body the BMF should list",
            "no exemption of its own", "could not be identified"),
  recall = c("11 of 11", "30 of 34", "5 of 6", "3 of 8"),
  pct = c("100.0%", "88.2%", "83.3%", "37.5%"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tab(agree_tbl, col.names = c("human's class", "model agreed", ""))
```

Overall **49 of 59 — 83.1%** [71.5%, 90.5%], Cohen's kappa **0.724**. Four
cases the human marked unclear are excluded; a non-answer cannot agree or
disagree with anything.

Three of the ten disagreements exist only because this comparison maps the
human's "geography unclear" verdict to *recoverable*. All three are churches.
Dropping that hedge gives 87.5% and kappa 0.795 — the figure above keeps the
conservative reading.

### The one class they diverge on is the reassuring part

37.5% on "could not be identified" looks alarming until the cases are read. Of
the 8 the human could not trace, the model agreed on exactly 3 — and those 3
are precisely the ones where it reported **low confidence and named no
organisation**.

On the other 5 it found something at medium or high confidence. `DOCKS TO
DOORWAYS` is a Belgrade Lakes Association campaign, and the filed street field
literally reads `PO Box 551 Belgrade Lakes Associati[on]`. `AMERICAN SHRINE
ASSOCIATES` sits at the Basilica of the National Shrine's address. `505 Main
Street Canton` is not a name at all, it is a street address, and the depot
there is run by a food pantry.

**The model's confidence tracks the disagreement exactly**: where it says low it
agrees the case is untraceable, and where it says medium or high it found what
the human could not. That is the opposite of the pattern the [MAYBE search
arm](adjudicating-maybe.html) showed, where confidence rose while accuracy
fell. Here confidence is worth routing on.

### On the EIN itself, which needs no vocabulary mapping

Both sides name an EIN on 24 cases and give **the same nine digits on 23 —
95.8%**. The exception is `The Salvation Army`: the model gives the Illinois
corporation, the human the Southern territory. Both EINs are real; which is
correct depends on which corporation received the money.

The model named an EIN on 11 cases where the human could not, and **all 11 are
in the reference** — 5 of them cases the human had already called a real
organisation without being able to produce its number.

The human named one where the model declined: `Hamilton Co Gen Hlt Dist`. It is
a county health district, the model called it government, and that EIN is the
one human EIN *not* in the reference. The model was right to refuse it.

### Both sides land in the same place

| | recoverable, of the same 63 |
|---|---:|
| human | 34 — 54.0% |
| model | 35 — 55.6% |

| | independently established EINs in the reference |
|---|---|
| model | **33 of 33 — 100%** |
| human | 24 of 25 — 96.0% |

Neither side found a single genuine coverage gap.



## Where that leaves the match rate

```{r}
tab(rate_tbl)
```

Recovering the NO tier is worth **+6.29 points**. But dropping the payees that
are not organisations the file could ever hold — ~492 identities, taking the
denominator from 4,868 to 4,376 — moves YES alone from 61.20% to **68.08%**, a
gain of **+6.88 points**, while matching precisely nothing.

The scope correction is worth more than the recovery. Only one of the two is a
matching improvement; the other is a statement about which grants were ever
answerable. Both should be reported, and neither should be quietly folded into
a headline.

## What this does not establish

- **Recoverability is not accuracy.** 36.3% of the tier has an EIN that exists
  in the reference. Whether it is the *correct* EIN rests on the head-to-head
  above and on the model's own confidence, not on the set-membership test.
- **The taxonomy is a model's judgement.** The mechanical parts — is the EIN in
  the reference, was it ever offered, what did it score — are not. The split
  between them is deliberate and the two should not be quoted with equal
  confidence.
- **One adjudicator on each side.** The human labels come from a single pass
  with no blind second review, and the model ran once at one effort level.
  Neither is a consensus.
- **`UNCERTAIN` was barely used.** One case of 100. A reviewer that almost
  never declines is either very well calibrated or is resolving ambiguity it
  should be surfacing; 100 cases cannot separate those.
- **The 120 never-scored identities are 12 cases in this sample.** Their
  composition is reported with everything else, but a 12-case subset supports
  no claim of its own.
- **Search cost is not in the token figure.** $0.0669 per case in tokens, plus
  3.2 web searches per case billed separately. No ratio to the MAYBE arms is
  quoted: those were computed on that experiment's own runs, some logged before
  the cache-write accounting was corrected.

## Reproducing

```
PFMATCH_DIR=. Rscript dev/adjudicate-10-no-packet.R    # re-runs the match, ~30 min
Rscript dev/adjudicate-11-no-search.R
Rscript dev/adjudicate-12-no-score.R

PF_NO_SET=cal Rscript dev/adjudicate-10-no-packet.R    # the human head-to-head
PF_NO_SET=cal Rscript dev/adjudicate-11-no-search.R
Rscript dev/adjudicate-14-no-calib.R
```

The packet stage gates every identity's tier against `BASELINE-2026-10C` and
stops on any drift, because a sample drawn from a drifted run does not describe
the baseline's NO tier and its recovery could not be added to the baseline's
match rate. It also re-checks that it drew the same 100 ids as the cached
packet, so a rebuild cannot silently leave collected verdicts keyed to
different case text.

Design, full read-out and the taxonomy definitions are in
`dev/NO-TIER-EXPERIMENT.md`; the reviewer's instructions are
`dev/LLM-NO-INSTRUCTIONS.md`.
